item.title: Narita Unagi Guide: Best Eel Restaurants & Access
item.description: The temple town of Narita is one of the best places near Tokyo to feast on unagi (freshwater eel) — a tradition stretching back centuries to feed pilgrims visiting Narita-san. Along the atmospheric Omotesando approach to the temple, dozens of long-established eel restaurants fillet, skewer and grill eel fresh to order, often in full view of the street, then glaze it in sweet-savoury tare sauce over rice as unadon or unaju.

item.title: Naritasan Calligraphy Guide: Shodo Experience & Access
item.description: The temple town of Narita is a wonderful place to try shodo (Japanese calligraphy) — the meditative art of writing characters with brush and ink. Narita-san is home to the Naritasan Calligraphy Museum, one of Japan’s leading museums devoted to the art, and the temple offers shakyo (sutra copying), where visitors trace or brush a Buddhist sutra in quiet concentration as a form of prayer and mindfulness. Hands-on brush workshops let you grind ink, learn the basic strokes and create your own piece to take home.

item.title: Naritasan Setsubun Guide: Bean-Throwing Festival & Access
item.description: Each February 3rd, Narita-san Shinshoji Temple hosts one of Japan’s most famous Setsubun celebrations — the bean-throwing ritual that drives out bad luck and welcomes spring. From a special stage, costumed participants hurl roasted soybeans (and lucky packets) to huge crowds shouting the traditional cry, and Narita-san is renowned for its celebrity guests: famous sumo grand champions, NHK taiga drama actors and other stars take part, drawing big crowds and national TV coverage.

item.title: Chiba Power Spots: Sacred Shrines, Ancient Temples & Spiritual Landscapes
item.description: Chiba Prefecture sits at a significant intersection in Japan’s spiritual geography. The Boso Peninsula was one of the last parts of the Kanto region to come under central authority, and its forested interior sheltered religious traditions that predate the Nara period. At the northern end, Naritasan commands one of the largest religious followings in the country. At the tip of the Boso, ancient clan shrines maintain rituals practiced without interruption for over a thousand years.

item.title: Top Sightseeing in Chiba: Naritasan, Nokogiri-yama & the Boso Peninsula
item.description: Chiba wraps around the east side of Tokyo Bay and extends far into the Pacific, forming a prefecture that most international visitors enter — through Narita Airport — and immediately leave. That is a mistake. Within Chiba’s borders you will find one of Japan’s most-visited Buddhist temples, a cliff-face Buddha larger than the one at Nara, a coastal town that turns its stone staircases into a river of traditional dolls each spring, and a forested gorge whose cave produces one of Japan’s most photographed natural phenomena.
